content.title: About
content.content: Dried peaches are the dehydrated fruit of the peach tree (Prunus persica) after the pit has been removed and the flesh dried. They retain a sweet, slightly caramelized flavor and a soft yet chewy texture. Dried peaches are commonly used in baking, granola, salads, or enjoyed as a snack on their own.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peach belongs to the Rosaceae family and is closely related to apricot, plum, and cherry.
When stored properly, dried peaches can last up to a year, making them a convenient fruit reserve for winter months.
Historically, dried peaches were a staple source of energy for travelers in ancient Mediterranean cultures.
In Japan, dried peaches are often served during tea ceremonies alongside green tea.
The sugar concentration in dried peaches is higher than in fresh fruit due to water removal.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Dried peaches contain beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance and normal heart function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and vitamin C in dried peaches protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: Vitamins A and C contribute to collagen synthesis, improving skin elasticity and tone.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Because the water is removed, dried peaches are relatively high in sugar and should be consumed in moderation by people monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Peach allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peaches, ranging from itching to swelling or breathing difficulties.

items.title: Sulfite content
items.content: Sulfites are sometimes added to preserve color; sulfite‑sensitive individuals may experience headaches or asthma symptoms.

items.title: Added preservatives
items.content: Commercial varieties may contain added sugars or sweeteners, increasing calorie density.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried peaches can be eaten as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used in sauces. For hot dishes, soaking them in warm water briefly restores some moisture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried peaches in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth and flavor loss. Discard any pieces that show signs of mold, off‑odors, or extreme dryness.
